His death, together with his brother Nadab, for offering 'strange fire' (esh zarah) before the LORD (Lev 10:1-2) became one of the Old Testament's most sobering warnings about the holiness demanded in worship. The incident is recalled repeatedly in Numbers and 1 Chronicles as a paradigm of priestly accountability. All twelve occurrences refer to the same individual."
